# std.app

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Application operations: a feature's significant entry points as typed
values with a stable identity, and the invocation metadata that travels
along a call chain (FRAMEWORK_DESIGN.md §7).

    let create = app.from_fn({ id: #orders/create, version: 1, doc: "Create an order." },
        fn(call, input: CreateOrder) -> Result<Order, Error> { store.insert(input) })
    let order = create.call(app.call(), { title: "first" })?

An operation is built only by `from_fn` or `from_pipeline`; it keeps the
input, output, error, and effect types of what it wraps, so typed
callers call it directly. `index` collects operations' metadata (for
routing, documentation, and tools) without erasing their types.

## Types

### `Actor`

```badger
pub type Actor = { id: String, roles: List<String> }
```

Who a call acts for, once an identity adapter has verified it.

### `Call`

```badger
struct Call { pub id: String, pub correlation: String, pub parent: Option<String>, pub operation: Option<Symbol>, pub deadline: Option<Instant>, pub actor: Option<{id: String, roles: List<String>}> }
```

Invocation metadata: small and immutable. A call has its own identity, a
correlation shared by the whole chain, the call it was made from, the
operation it entered, an optional deadline, and an optional verified
actor. It carries no dependencies: those are typed parameters.

#### `Call.acting_for`

```badger
fn acting_for(self: &Self, actor: Actor) -> Call
```

The call acting for a verified actor (for identity adapters).

#### `Call.child`

```badger
fn child(self: &Self, operation: Symbol) -> Call !{Io}
```

The call a nested invocation of `operation` makes: a new identity,
this call as its parent, and the same correlation, deadline, and actor.

#### `Call.expired`

```badger
fn expired(self: &Self) -> Bool !{Io}
```

Has the deadline passed?

#### `Call.remaining`

```badger
fn remaining(self: &Self) -> Option<Duration> !{Io}
```

The time left before the deadline (`none` without one).

#### `Call.within`

```badger
fn within(self: &Self, limit: Duration) -> Call !{Io}
```

The call with a deadline `limit` from now, unless it already has an
earlier one: a deadline can be shortened, never extended.

### `Error`

```badger
struct Error { pub code: Symbol, pub message: String }
```

A problem with operation metadata.

#### `Error.display`

```badger
fn display(self: &Self) -> String
```

### `Index`

```badger
struct Index { entries: List<{id: Symbol, version: Int, doc: String}> }
```

Validated metadata of a set of operations: identities unique, versions
positive, documentation present. Typed operations stay with the features
that export them; the index refers to them by identity.

#### `Index.find`

```badger
fn find(self: &Self, id: Symbol) -> Option<Info>
```

The metadata of the operation `id`.

#### `Index.operations`

```badger
fn operations(self: &Self) -> List<Info>
```

Every operation's metadata, in registration order.

### `Info`

```badger
pub type Info = { id: Symbol, version: Int, doc: String }
```

An operation's stable identity and documentation.

### `Operation`

```badger
struct Operation<I, O, E, Eff> { pub info: {id: Symbol, version: Int, doc: String}, invoke: fn(app.Call, I) -> Result<O, E> }
```

A typed operation: `invoke` receives the call (with this operation as
its `operation`) and the input.

#### `Operation.call`

```badger
fn call(self: &Self, caller: Call, input: I) -> Result<O, E> !{Io, Eff}
```

Invoke the operation as a nested call of `caller`, in the caller's task.

## Functions

### `call`

```badger
fn call() -> Call !{Io}
```

A new root call (no parent, no deadline, no actor).

### `call_within`

```badger
fn call_within(limit: Duration) -> Call !{Io}
```

A root call that must finish within `limit`.

### `from_fn`

```badger
fn from_fn<I, O, E, Eff>(info: Info, f: fn(Call, I) -> Result<O, E> !Eff) -> Operation<I, O, E, Eff>
```

An operation from a function of the call and the input.

### `from_pipeline`

```badger
fn from_pipeline<I, O, E, Eff>(info: Info, plan: pipeline.Plan<{ call: Call, input: I }, O, E, Eff>) -> Operation<I, O, E, Eff>
```

An operation from a pipeline whose input context is `{ call, input }`:
its stages see both, and its handler's reply is the operation's output.

### `index`

```badger
fn index(infos: List<Info>) -> Result<Index, Error>
```
